answer.evidence: The transcription's header is '14 ONE WAY TO CULTIVATE COURAGE.' It opens with 'armed at all points and disciplined to meet any' and ends with 'is “ something in it,” and feel also a conviction that'. The same header is at the top of leaf 104, that opening line is its first line and that closing line is its last line.

The transcription only says 'blank flyleaf or endpaper... No text or illustrations are present.' Two leaves fit that: p240 and p244 are both empty pages. p241 itself is a tissue guard with the Plate LVII text showing through from behind, so it is not truly blank. With no text to compare, the transcription cannot be tied to p240 rather than p244.

The heading 'THE ROMANCE OF TWO CAMERAS.' and the opening line 'T was in the old Spanish town of Toledo' are at the top of p139. The last line, '"The Señor is incredulous," said the courier', closes its right column. The footer 'Vol. XL.—16.' and folio 117 are at the bottom.

The transcription begins with 'ad eterna atque interiora converteret. Venite inquit ad me omnes' at the top of the left column of p92. It also has the heading 'Capitulum. viii.' in the middle of the left column, and it ends with 'Itaque qui fratres quos videt non diligit: deus' at the bottom of the right column. The page shows the running head 'Liber' and has no printed folio number.

The transcription opens with "purpose. It comes from the Supreme Power." and ends with "to be dominated, brow-beaten or cheated by others". These are the first and last lines of the leaf, under the running head "SOME PRACTICAL MENTAL RECIPES. 5".

The transcription's 'Thus the testimony to the great revival of beleef im reincarmation could be prolonged for many pages' matches the start of the right column, below the verse 'Dust that was flesh of mine moulders in many a tomb'. Its 'PHILIP HENDERSON' signature is at the foot of the right column. Its 'sings / ogress of the soul / riumphalis' matches the cut-off Bliss Carman lines in the left column.

The transcription only says 'blank page' and has no text to compare. Several leaves fit that: p120 and p124 are blank, and p121 is a tissue leaf with only reversed show-through of the 'PLATE XXVII' text. So the transcription can't pick out one leaf.

The heading 'MENTAL INTEMPERANCE.' and the opening 'TEMPERANCE means the proper use of force.' appear at the top of the p27 leaf. Its last line is 'to swell the great current of anger; and you are', and the footer reads 'Thoughts are Things.' This is the opening page of the chapter and has no printed page number. The next leaf, p28 (folio 2), continues with 'also receiving from...'

The transcription opens with "BAR-LOCK TYPEWRITER.", which is the heading at the top of leaf 238 under the "Writing Machines" banner. It closes with "Minneapolis, Minn.", the last line of the Smith Premier branch-office list at the bottom right of that leaf.

The transcription opens with "had eaten their fill or were hungry, they would be pleased or vexed." That is the first line of p529, under the header "Sacrifices to the Departed. 515". It ends with "how can people firmly believe in this?", which closes the text on that leaf, and the signature 33* is at the bottom. The leaf labelled p530 is folio 516, which begins CHAPTER XLII "Sacrifices (Chi-yi)".

The transcription starts at '5. Alavivo et Fritigerno ad convivium corrogatis', which is the first line of the leaf after 'cendit.'. It ends with 'Barbarique, hoc contemplato, globos', the last line of the leaf. The header 'VAL. GRATIAN. ET VALENT. II. 376.' and page number 519 also match.

The transcription is only '<page-type>blank</page-type>' and has no text. Pages 56 and 60 are blank. Page 57 has no printed text of its own, only mirror-image show-through of the Plate XI caption and picture. Pages 54, 55, 58 and 59 have Plate X/XI captions or pictures, so they don't match. With several blank leaves, the transcription can't be tied to one of them.

The transcription opens with "You may joke and put me off, but it 's a thing that cries for explanation." and breaks off at "Norrisson built a ditch s[…]". Both lines are on p93 (folio 711): the first at the top of the left column, the second at the bottom of the right column.

The transcription opens with "A New Model of the Universe. By P. D. OUSPENSKY". On p68 this is the top of the left column, under the header "732 THE ARYAN PATH [October". It ends with "We eagerly await the second and third volumes, T. N. S.", which is the bottom of the right column of the same leaf.

The running head 'THOUGHT OF ENLIGHTENMENT 87' matches the top of p91. The first line, 'the struggle for the welfare of the mean body', is the first line of p91, and the last line, 'fellow-creatures are the same as himself. “ All', is its last line. 'Indra (43)' is in the lower middle of the page.

The text from 'common sort seemeth great, and that in respect of the Moones Orbe' (first line) to the heading 'What reasons moued Aristotle... Centre to the whole world.' and the closing 'Earths stabilitie in the middle or lowest part of the world,' with signature 'N 2' matches p111 and p113. Those two leaves are identical duplicate scans, so they cannot be told apart. p112 is a duplicate of p110, which starts 'Trismegistus calleth him the visible God', and does not match.

Opens 'Fall auch nicht gleich finden zu können' and closes 'Weit entfernt, rief ich aus, dem Kaiser anzugehören, darf'. These are the first and last lines of the leaf headed '36 ITALIENISCHE REISE I'.

The transcription opens with "It is Interesting ... THE CENTURY DICTIONARY" and ends with "THE CENTURY CO., 33 East 17th St., New York. June, '90." Both match leaf 231, which has the BOOKS header and folio 69. The heading is at the top of that leaf and the address and date are at the bottom.

The running head 'LIFE AND WORK OF ALAN LEO 131' and the opening line 'and methodical, in temperament he was a' are at the top of leaf p139. The closing line 'brooding over the world. " I can always' is at the bottom of the same leaf.

The transcription is the cover of No. 11, Vol. V ('THE FOUNDING OF ... MACHA (continued) ... 201', 'Charlotte E. Woods 215', 'DUBLIN: 13, Eustace Street'). Leaves p251 and p253 both show this same cover. They look like duplicate scans, with the same contents list and the same stain near 'AUGUST 15TH, 1897', so the text cannot tell which leaf it renders.

The transcription reads 'This page is blank.' / 'blank page'. Leaf p26 is the only blank one here. It has no printed text, folio or running head, only faint show-through and a stain at the lower left. Every other leaf has printed text: p23–p25 are folios 11–13 of 'Some Laws of Health and Beauty', and p27–p29 are the 'Mental Intemperance' chapter (folios 1–3).

The transcription has no text, only '<page-type>blank</page-type>'. Pages 296 and 300 are fully blank. Page 297 is a tissue guard that shows only mirrored PLATE LXXI text bleeding through from page 298. Several leaves fit a blank-page transcription equally well, so it cannot be tied to one of them.

The transcription has no text. It only says 'page-type: blank' and 'blank flyleaf or endpaper'. Several leaves here have no printed content: p212 and p216 are completely blank, and p213 is a blank leaf with mirrored show-through of Plate L from p214. A blank transcription cannot tell these leaves apart.

The transcription begins 'CALIFORNI A— Winter Season, 1801-02', which matches the headline at the top of this leaf, right under the HOTELS banner. It ends 'G. & C. MERRIAM & CO., Springfield, Mass.', which matches the bottom of the Webster's dictionary ad in the lower right.

The transcription contains no text, only "blank page, flyleaf" and "No text or illustrations are present". Pages 216, 217 and 220 have no printed text of their own. Page 217 shows only mirrored bleed-through of the Plate LI text, page 216 is plain cream paper, and page 220 is a blank brown backing sheet. Nothing in the transcription picks out one of these leaves.

Running head 'Mental Medicine' and folio 73 at the top. The text opens 'itself, and reassert itself with greater and greater power' and closes 'effect of the elements on your body. Every moment' at the bottom of leaf p79.

The transcription says only 'This page is blank.' Leaf p32 is the only blank leaf in pages 30-36. It has no text, no folio and no picture, just a faint watermark line at the top. Leaf p33 is not blank: it is printed page 19, which begins 'ONE may ask: "How can we best help humanity?' and ends with the note '(From Katherine Tingley's Brief Address...)'.

The transcription opens with the headings 'SUHRAWARDI / THE APOSTLE OF ILLUMINATION' and the editors' note '[Dr. Margaret Smith contributed...'. These are at the top of leaf 46. It ends with 'al-Zahir, a son of the Sultan', which is the last line of that leaf's right column. The leaf has no printed page number (it would be 710).

The transcription's opening line 'AND COMFORT, ARE NOW THROWN OUT TO "WASTE AND DECAY."' is the first line of the text on this leaf. Its closing footnote 18, 'The following queries were sent to the Rev. Mr. Benjamin Allen ... were employed last wi[nter]', is at the bottom of the leaf. The running head 'Address delivered before the' also matches. The transcription reads the folio as '58', but the leaf shows '38'.

The transcription says only 'This page is blank.' and has no text, heading, folio or picture to match. Pages 28 and 32 are fully blank. Page 29 is a tissue guard with no print of its own; only Plate IV shows through faintly from the leaves behind it. A blank rendering fits several leaves equally well, so it cannot pick out one.

The transcription only says 'There is no text or imagery present on this page.' Leaves 252 and 256 are both completely blank. Leaf 253 is a tissue guard with no printing of its own; only the Plate LX caption from 254 shows through, reversed. All three fit the description equally well, so the transcription cannot be matched to one leaf.

The running head '1916 BEAUTIES OF THE QURÂN 523' is at the top of the leaf. Below it, the first quotation begins 'Walk not proudly on the earth...'. The last line at the foot of the leaf is 'and by following the precepts of the Qurân.'

The transcription opens with 'Besant, Annie (continued)' and 'Free Trade v. "Fair" Trade' at the top of p39 (folio 7) and closes with 'Water, I., Water, II., 1d. each; or in wrapper, 4d. Four', which is the last line on that leaf

The transcription begins with the running head 'CHILLS" 589' and the line '"Tryin' to."', which is the top of the left column on p125. It ends with 'again 's long 's I live."', the last line of the right column on the same leaf.

The transcription opens with 'gions, gods created by man in his own image', which is the top of the left column on leaf 79. It ends with 'which will appear in an early', which is the bottom of the right column. The running head '1931] ENDS AND SAYINGS 271' also matches that leaf.

The transcription opens with 'wells outside of the town, we entered the khan and pitched the tent', which is the first line of leaf p260 under the header '252 THE LANDS OF THE SARACEN.' It ends with 'we overlooked an immense plain, uncultivated, appa-', which is the last line of that leaf. Leaf p261 is folio 253 and starts 'rently unfertile'.

The transcription contains no text, only '<page-type>blank</page-type>' and 'blank flyleaf or endpaper'. Leaf 105 is not blank: it has mirrored show-through of the PLATE XXIII caption and picture. Leaves 104 and 108 are both blank, so the transcription could match either one.

The transcription begins "are due to the lightness and exhilaration coming of" and ends "in the body of a man or woman child. It might not". These are the first and last text lines on the leaf that has the running head "RE-EMBODIMENT UNIVERSAL IN NATURE. 3" and the footer "Thoughts are Things."

The transcription only says the page is blank ('<page-type>blank</page-type>') and has no text to compare. More than one leaf here could match that. p264 and p268 are fully blank. p265 is a tissue guard with no printed text of its own; the Plate LXIII text and drawing only show through from the next leaf. p262, p263, p266 and p267 have plate text or drawings, so they don't match. The transcription says only 'blank page'. Leaves p188 and p192 are blank, and p189 shows only mirrored bleed-through of the Plate XLIV captions from p190. So several leaves fit, and the transcription has no text to tell them apart.

The transcription says '<page-type>blank</page-type>' and 'This is a blank page'. Leaf 120 is the only blank leaf in the set: it has no printed text, folio or picture, only a faint watermark line at the top. Leaf 121 has printed text ('THOSE who have striven the most...', folio 99), so the transcription is filed one leaf too late.

The transcription runs from 'Unsurpassed wearing quality, with a finish like silk' (the Cleanfast Black Stockings ad, top left) to 'HALL'S BAZAR FORM CO. ... 833 Broadway, New-York, and 139 Regent Street, London' (bottom of the page). It also has 'WALKING MADE EASY' and 'STERN BROTHERS ... NEW PARIS CORSET' in between. All of these are on the Dry Goods page with folio 65.

The transcription is marked page-type 'blank' with a note about 'faint show-through from the reverse side'. Leaf p24 is the only blank leaf in this run. It shows faint show-through and has no folio. Leaf p25, which the transcription is stored under, is printed: it has the heading 'WHERE YOU TRAVEL WHEN YOU SLEEP.' and folio 1.

The transcription's '<page-num>57</page-num>' and '<margin>Cap 24</margin>' match leaf p52, which has folio 57 at the top left and 'Cap 24' in the left margin at about line 4. No other leaf has these. The 20 near-identical romanized lines look like a hallucinated rendering, not a real reading of the script.

The transcription starts with 'A mus, solus omnium spondylorum (ut diximus) utriusque productionis fines mediocriter devexos', which matches the first line under the header 'CORPORIS HVMANI LIB. XIII. 199' on p983. Its ending, 'sed pro iis declives habuerunt proximis lumbi spondylis adsimiles' followed by '*Cur prima Col…', matches the line just before the 'Cur prima Colli Vertebra' (CAP. 3) heading near the foot of p983. The catchword 'Porro' also matches. p984 has the header 'DE VSV PARTIVM' and begins 'Porro, attendas animum'.

The transcription opens with the heading 'NEW BOOKS AND OLD / RACE RELATIONS*' at the top of p47. Its body text ends at the foot of the right column with 'of the Southern Whites with regard to the Negro:—', and the footnote '*Race Relations: Adjustment of Whites and Negroes in the United States, By Willis D. Weatherford...' is at the bottom of the same leaf. No folio is printed on this leaf; going by its neighbours (510 and 512), it would be 511.

Header 'EXPOSITION DU SYSTÈME GRAPHIQUE MAYA. 23'. The text opens with '« ces pierres qu'ils conservaient leur histoire et établissaient toute espèce de « calculs. »' at the top of leaf 39 and ends with 'Les conquérants espagnols les trouvèrent au Mexique,' on its last line. Leaf 39 also has the same six footnotes: Velasco, Ibid. pag. 116, Origen de los Indios, Chronica del Peru, Coronica moralizada, Balboa. Leaf 40 is printed page 24 and starts 'comme les Portugais en Chine'.

The transcription only says "blank flyleaf or endpaper... No text or illustrations". Pages 144 and 148 are both fully blank and look the same. Page 145 has no printed text of its own, only the reversed show-through of Plate XXXIII through a tissue guard. Nothing in the transcription tells these leaves apart.

The transcription is just a blank-page record ('No text or illustrations are present on this side of the leaf'). Several leaves fit that: p164 and p168 are blank, and p165 shows only bleed-through of the Plate XXXVIII caption and picture from the other side. Nothing in the transcription tells these apart. The other leaves have content the transcription leaves out: p162 (Plate XXXVII text), p163 (Plate XXXVII A/B pictures), p166 (Plate XXXVIII Gita Govinda caption) and p167 (Plate XXXVIII picture).

The header 'THEBAID, XII. 748-776', the opening line 'riding aloft in four-horsed car' and the closing line 'through a thousand meshes spirts upward' all match leaf p513, which has printed folio 501. Leaf p514 is the Latin page with folio 502.

The heading 'THE PROCESS OF RE-EMBODIMENT.' and the opening line 'The fact that one person may gain such a mesmeric control' are at the top of leaf 143, which is the chapter's first page and has no printed number. Its last line, 'The highest character of which you are capable of conceiving has a repre-', is at the bottom of the same leaf, above the 'Thoughts are Things.' footer.

Opens 'et medios sermones intercipiant et omnia tumultu confundant' and closes 'disponendum fuisset. Nam quod fideliter firmum'. These match the first and last lines of p520, which has the QUINTILIAN header and folio 508.

The transcription opens with 'of it appears alive, and are seemingly of the same Kind' and ends with 'afterwards to the Royal Society *.' followed by the note '* Philof. Tranf. No. 478.' This matches leaf p283 (folio 245), which has the running head 'Eels in Paste viviparous', signature R 3 and catchword 'I'. Leaf p284 (folio 246) starts with 'I first saw the Experiment with Mr. Sherwood' instead.

The transcription opens with 'Imperial Parliament Series — Uniform, crown 8vo' and ends with 'Kossuth, Louis — Memories of my Exile'. On leaf p56 (printed page 24), the first is the opening entry at the top and the second is the last entry at the bottom.

The transcription opens with 'soon as Paka saw this, he gave his daughter a sound scolding', which is the first line under the header '192 POLYNESIAN MYTHOLOGY' on leaf p210. It ends with 'by the time it was full daybreak', which is that leaf's last line. The leaf labelled p211 is printed page 193 and starts 'they had reached Waitakaruru'.

The transcription opens with "Christopher Columbus, And how he received and imparted the Spirit of Discovery" right under the BOOKS 2 header, and ends with "Houghton, Mifflin & Company, 4 Park St. Boston". Both match the top and bottom of leaf p12. Leaf p13 is the Marcus Ward's booklets ad, printed page 3.

The transcription only says 'blank page' and has no text. Three leaves fit that: p68 and p72 are blank, and p69 has only a faint mirrored show-through of the Plate XIV caption and picture, with no real print. A blank transcription can't be matched to just one of them.

The transcription opens with the headings 'THE BRITISH IN INDIA / MATERIAL SUCCESS AND SPIRITUAL FAILURE' and the editors' note about Robert Sencourt. These match the top of leaf p52. Its last words, 'her own culture and religion', match the bottom of the right column on that leaf. No page number is printed on this article's opening page. The pages before it are numbered 241-243 and the next one is 245, so it would be page 244.

The transcription opens with "results of the previous deeds, the Intellect (Buddhi) could not help but yield to the Mind" and closes with "the functions of the Intel-lect are: (1) To analyze the subjects collected". These match the first and last lines of leaf p71 (folio 45, header 'The Ascent of Man.'). Leaf p72 is folio 46 and opens with "by the Mind through the help of the Sense Forces".

The running head 'Philadelphia Agricultural Society. 35' is at the top of the leaf. The opening line 'Scotland, of the single article of cotton goods' starts the text block, and the heading 'IV. State of the Nation.' sits in the upper half. Footnote 17 ('Mr. Webster was so happy...') closes the page, ending with 'Mr. Webster's speech as originally reported.'

The transcription opens with "its mixture of good and evil: Erinnys, Fates and Furies" and ends with "Heine and Musset toyed with the devil's machinations; and Goethe". These match the top of the left column and the bottom of the right column on the leaf with the header 502 THE ARYAN PATH [August.

The transcription says only 'This page is blank.' Pages 40 and 44 are both blank. Page 41 has nothing printed on it either, only mirrored show-through of the Plate VII caption and image. Any of these could be the leaf, so there is nothing to decide between them.

The heading 'CHAPTER V / WATCHFULNESS' and the opening line 'He who would keep the rules must diligently' are at the top of leaf 57. Its last line, 'If the Perfect Charity frees the world from', sits just above the printed folio 53 at the bottom.

The transcription is just '[This page is blank.]'. Leaf p7 is not blank: it has the contents page for August 1903. Leaves p4, p5 and p6 are all blank, so the transcription could belong to any of them.

The transcription starts with 'The kingdom of mind is full of tyrants.' and ends with 'You commence thinking in part with the'. Both lines match the first and last text lines of leaf p124, which has the running head '4 THE SLAVERY OF FEAR.' and the footer 'Thoughts are Things.'

Its text runs from 'We are through our mental conditions always drawing things...' to '...might be evident to our spiritual or finer senses', and the footer reads 'Calm demand brings all good things in time.' Leaf p12 is a different page: it carries printed folio 2 and starts 'were they developed.' The leaf p11 has no printed page number.

The transcription says the page is blank ('(This page is blank.)', page-type blank). Only one of the seven leaves is blank: p96, the back of Plate VIII, with no page number. p97 is printed page 61 and is full of text ('LATIN 61', XXXII. Letter to a Tribunus Militum), so the transcription doesn't match it.

The transcription says only 'blank page' and has no text. p300 and p304 are completely blank. p301 is also blank apart from reversed show-through of the Plate LXXII text on p302. All three leaves fit equally well, so the transcription cannot pick out one of them.

The running head 'THE LOVE OF RIGHT' with folio 77 matches. The opening line 'to boundless anguish, and why does my bosom' is at the top of leaf p81, and the closing line 'their lustrous forms grow nurtured by the Conqueror's sweet melody ; then they issue in comely' is at the bottom.

The transcription has no text, only page-type 'blank'. Leaves p160 and p164 are both blank with no printed text or folio. Leaf p161 is a tissue guard that shows only reversed show-through of Plate XXXVII and has no text of its own. Several leaves match equally well, so the transcription cannot be tied to one of them.

The transcription starts with 'and love are so near akin as poets feign', which is the first line under the running head 'A Vindication of the Rights of Woman'. It ends with 'who make man feel for man, independent of the station', the last line. The folio 103 is at the bottom.

The transcription has no printed text, only 'Marbled paper endleaf featuring a swirling pattern of blue, red, and yellow pigments'. Leaves 610 and 611 are both marbled endpapers that match this description, so the leaves cannot decide it. Leaf 608 is a blank leaf with show-through, 609 has a Harvard bookplate and 612 is the leather cover.

The transcription says only '<page-type>blank</page-type>' and has no text. Several leaves fit that: p304 and p308 are blank, and p305 has no printed text of its own, only faint show-through of the Plate LXXIII captions. A blank transcription can't tell these leaves apart.

'consciousness in the second of the super-physical worlds' opens leaf p253 (folio 237, header RESURRECTION AND ASCENSION), and 'consciousness in its appropriate region' closes it; p254 is folio 238 and begins 'This conception should be readily enough grasped.'
